# Ceres - the build root.
#
# One single source of truth for which files make up the project. There used to be three that
# didn't talk to each other (two hand-maintained .vcxproj files, tests/build.sh with globs, and a
# g++ line in CI), and with six projects that would be eighteen lists to keep in sync.
#
# The Visual Studio .vcxproj is now generated by CMake instead of hand-written:
#     cmake --preset msvc && cmake --build --preset msvc-debug
#
# During the migration the directories are empty on purpose. Each library still builds - with a
# placeholder translation unit that disappears on its own as soon as there's a real .cpp in its
# src/ - so the tree configures and compiles from day one and code can be moved file by file
# without leaving the branch broken along the way.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.28)

project(Ceres
    VERSION      0.1.0
    DESCRIPTION  "A 32-bit virtual machine and its assembler"
    HOMEPAGE_URL "https://github.com/Krampus1721/CeresASM"
    LANGUAGES    CXX)

# C++23 across the whole tree, with no compiler extensions: what compiles here compiles with
# MSVC, GCC and Clang, which is exactly what uncovered the four missing headers back when MSVC
# was the only compiler that ever saw this code.
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/cmake")

# Only makes sense when Ceres is the top-level project; if it's ever included from another tree,
# whoever's in charge there decides where the binaries go and whether tests get built.
if(PROJECT_IS_TOP_LEVEL)
    set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin")
    set(CMAKE_ARCHIVE_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/lib")
    set(CMAKE_LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/lib")
    set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY USE_FOLDERS ON)
    set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY PREDEFINED_TARGETS_FOLDER "cmake")
endif()

option(CERES_BUILD_TESTS      "Build the test suites"                 ${PROJECT_IS_TOP_LEVEL})
option(CERES_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS "Treat warnings as errors"             OFF)
option(CERES_ENABLE_IPO "Enable interprocedural optimization for release builds" OFF)
# Opt-in only: -mpopcnt/-mbmi (GCC/Clang) or /arch:AVX2 (MSVC) let opcodes like POPCNT/CLZ/CTZ
# (execution_engine.h, backed by std::popcount/std::countl_zero/std::countr_zero) compile to a
# single native instruction instead of falling back to library sequences on the generic x86-64
# baseline. Never turned on for a binary that gets distributed: it raises the minimum CPU the
# result will run on, which -O2/-O3 alone never does.
option(CERES_ENABLE_ARCH_TUNING "Enable target-CPU instruction tuning for release builds (not portable to older CPUs)" OFF)

# Profile-guided optimization, GCC/Clang only for now (see CeresSettings.cmake for why MSVC's
# /LTCG:PGInstrument + /LTCG:PGOptimize workflow isn't wired here yet). Two builds, not one:
# configure+build with CERES_PGO_GENERATE, run a representative workload (libs/vm/benchmarks is
# the one already in the tree), then reconfigure the *same* CERES_PGO_DIR with CERES_PGO_USE and
# rebuild. Mutually exclusive - CeresSettings.cmake errors out if both are set at once.
option(CERES_PGO_GENERATE "Instrument this build to record a profile for a later CERES_PGO_USE build" OFF)
option(CERES_PGO_USE "Optimize this build using a profile previously recorded with CERES_PGO_GENERATE" OFF)
set(CERES_PGO_DIR "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/pgo" CACHE PATH "Where PGO profile data is written to (CERES_PGO_GENERATE) or read from (CERES_PGO_USE) - must be the same path across both builds")

if(CERES_ENABLE_IPO)
    include(CheckIPOSupported)
    check_ipo_supported(RESULT CERES_IPO_SUPPORTED OUTPUT CERES_IPO_ERROR LANGUAGES CXX)
    if(NOT CERES_IPO_SUPPORTED)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "CERES_ENABLE_IPO was requested, but the compiler does not support it: ${CERES_IPO_ERROR}")
    endif()
    set(CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION_RELEASE ON)
endif()

include(CeresSettings)
include(CeresLibrary)

if(CERES_BUILD_TESTS)
    enable_testing()
    # Before the libraries: ceres_add_tests() checks for the runner's target, and an
    # if(TARGET ...) check is evaluated on the spot, not at generate time.
    add_subdirectory(tests/framework)
endif()

# The order follows the dependency graph: nothing is declared before what it depends on.
add_subdirectory(libs/core)
add_subdirectory(libs/vm)
add_subdirectory(libs/devices)
add_subdirectory(libs/asm)
add_subdirectory(libs/debug)
add_subdirectory(apps/cli)

if(CERES_BUILD_TESTS)
    add_subdirectory(tests/e2e)
endif()

if(PROJECT_IS_TOP_LEVEL)
    ceres_report_migration_status()
endif()
